question.text: By how many percentage points will Okta (OKTA) outperform or underperform the software ETF IGV between the October 30 and November 13, 2026 market closes?
question.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves from Okta's (ticker OKTA) return minus the return of the iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF (ticker IGV) over the period from the October 30, 2026 regular-session close to the November 13, 2026 regular-session close, expressed in percentage points. Both returns are computed from the "Close" column of the daily historical tables at https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/OKTA/history/ and https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/IGV/history/.

Value = [100 × (OKTA close on Nov 13, 2026 ÷ OKTA close on Oct 30, 2026)] − [100 × (IGV close on Nov 13, 2026 ÷ IGV close on Oct 30, 2026)], i.e. OKTA's percent change minus IGV's percent change. For example, if OKTA rises 5% and IGV rises 2% over the period, the question resolves as 3; if OKTA falls 4% while IGV rises 1%, it resolves as -5.

If either table has no November 13, 2026 row (for example because the exchange was closed for the whole session), the most recent session before November 14, 2026 that appears in both tables is used for both tickers. If the Yahoo Finance pages are unavailable, the corresponding "Close" values at https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/okta/history/ and https://stockanalysis.com/etf/igv/history/ are used; if both sites are unavailable, [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) will be used.
question.fine_print: Only regular-session closing prices from the two tables are used; pre-market, after-hours and "Adj Close" values do not count. Both legs must be computed over the same pair of sessions.

- 2026-11-02: OKTA closed at $184.87 (-11.22%) on 5.9M shares. IGV closed at $101.90 (-2.29%).
- 2026-11-03: OKTA closed at $189.68 (+2.60%) on 33.8M shares, roughly 6 to 10 times its normal volume. That spike is most likely index funds buying at the close ahead of its S&P 500 entry on Nov 4. IGV closed at $102.66 (+0.75%).
- Value so far as of Nov 3: OKTA is down 8.91% and IGV is down 1.56%, so the running value is about **-7.35 pp**.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. There are 8 trading sessions left (Nov 4 to Nov 13).
- OKTA starts about 7 pp behind. Recovering that gap would need OKTA to beat IGV by roughly 8% from here, measured against the new lower base.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-04: Okta joins the S&P 500 at the open, replacing Kenvue. It moves out of the MidCap 400. [Teleborsa](https://www.teleborsa.it/News/2026/11/02/okta-sostituira-kenvue-nell-indice-s-p-500-143.html), [Yahoo](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/dear-okta-stock-fans-mark-151951934.html)

- 2026-11-02: Okta, Zscaler, Qualys, Rapid7 and SentinelOne all fell together. StockStory blamed:
  - Oracle filing to raise $20B
  - Alphabet and Amazon capex squeezing free cash flow
  - Check Point's sales miss
  - Fortinet's weak bookings
  
  The article doesn't mention the DHS breach. Even so, Okta fell 11.2%, much more than its peers' morning moves of 3 to 6%. [FinancialContent/StockStory](https://www.financialcontent.com/article/stockstory-2026-11-2-okta-zscaler-qualys-rapid7-and-sentinelone-shares-plummet-what-you-need-to-know), [GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9163614/okta-inc-okta-shares-fall-112-gf-value-says-still-overvalued)

No source I found shows DHS confirming that Okta was the access route. [Nextgov](https://www.nextgov.com/cybersecurity/2026/10/dhs-personnel-leak-exposes-contact-details-and-sensitive-job-information/416901/), [Yahoo](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/okta-okta-tied-data-leak-221128500.html), [CBC](https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/dhs-data-breach-leak-distributed-denial-of-secrets-9.7400488), [breached.company](https://breached.company/dhs-leak-exposes-about-40-000-employees-after-hacker-claims/), [pasqualepillitteri.it](https://pasqualepillitteri.it/en/news/27968/dhs-data-breach-40000-employees-okta-denies), [tokencore](https://www.tokencore.com/blog/the-dhs-breach-is-a-warning-to-every-okta-customer)

## 4. Base rates and volatility
These are my own calculations from the October daily tables.
- In October, OKTA moved more than 5% in a day on 7 sessions. Its biggest days were -10.2% (Oct 16), +7.5% (Oct 21) and -6.45% (Oct 14).
- IGV's biggest daily moves were about 3 to 5% (-4.8% Oct 16, -3.5% Oct 29, -3.4% Oct 30).
- OKTA behaves like a high-beta version of IGV, about 2 to 3 times as volatile. Its daily moves relative to IGV were often 3 to 6 pp. Over 10 trading days, a rough standard deviation for the gap is around 8 to 12 pp.
- Example: on Oct 16 OKTA fell 10.2% and IGV fell 4.8%. By Oct 23 OKTA had recovered to $213, beating IGV's rebound.
- Past Okta incidents:
  - In Oct 2023, the support-system breach sent the stock down about 11% in one day, and it fell further when the scope was widened in Nov 2023. [Axios](https://www.axios.com/2023/11/29/okta-all-customers-affected-in-october-breach)
  - In Mar 2022 (LAPSUS$), it fell about 10% or more within a few days.
- S&P 500 additions: studies often find that newly added stocks give back some of their pre-inclusion run-up after the effective date. I didn't find anything specific to OKTA on this.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market on OKTA's price or its performance against IGV.
- Kalshi has markets on Okta's count of customers with over $100k in annual contract value, which resolve with the Dec 1 earnings, after this question. For Q3, "Above 5325" is priced at 0.62 and "Above 5350" at 0.28. These don't bear directly on the question.
- I found no analyst price-target changes tied to the DHS incident.

## 6. Upcoming events before Nov 13
- Nov 4: Okta's first day in the S&P 500. The heavy index buying on Nov 3 may unwind.
- Possible DHS or Okta updates on how the attackers got in. Confirmation that Okta itself was compromised, a congressional letter or a CISA advisory would be risks specific to Okta.
- Software and security earnings reported during the window could move the whole sector, IGV as well as OKTA. I didn't verify the exact dates.
- US macro data (CPI is likely around Nov 12 to 13; not verified) and the ongoing AI-capex and software-valuation rotation, which drove most of the moves since Oct 29.
- The Nov 13 close is a Friday. There's no market holiday that week.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left:** About 8 trading sessions (Nov 4 to Nov 13). The outcome is known at the Nov 13 close, around 22:00 UTC that day.

(b) **Latest known value:** As of the Nov 3, 2026 close (stockanalysis.com fallback), OKTA was at $189.68, down 8.91% from $208.24, and IGV was at $102.66, down 1.56% from $104.29. The running value is about **-7.35 pp**.

(c) **If nothing changed:** About -7.4 pp.

(d) **If the current trend continued:** OKTA lost about 9 pp relative to IGV on Nov 2 and gained back about 2 pp on Nov 3. Extending the high-beta selloff would push the value toward -12 to -15 pp. The recent pattern after sharp drops has been partial rebounds, as after Oct 16, so the trend signal is ambiguous.

(e) **Historical variation:** OKTA's daily moves relative to IGV are often 3 to 6 pp. Over 8 sessions, the standard deviation of the gap is roughly 7 to 10 pp. Event risk from the DHS breach story and the post-inclusion unwind fattens the tails, especially the lower one.

(f) **Expectations of experts and markets:** There is no market on this quantity and no analyst target changes tied to the incident. Two factors point in opposite directions:
- S&P 500 additions often give back gains after the effective date. The Nov 3 volume spike was index buying that may unwind, which is a mild negative.
- Oversold high-beta names often bounce, which is a mild positive.

The net effect is a median near the current value, with a slight negative tilt.

(g) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- **Low:** DHS or CISA confirms that the attackers got in through Okta's own systems, or a congressional inquiry follows. Combined with continued software de-rating, OKTA could fall another 15 to 20% while IGV is flat, giving around -25 to -30 pp.
- **High:** Investigators attribute the breach to stolen DHS credentials rather than an Okta flaw, and the software sector rebounds in a sharp risk-on rally. OKTA's high beta could then lift it 15 to 20% against IGV's 5 to 7%, giving around +8 to +13 pp.
